_doc: Short musical stingers made with the ElevenLabs Music API (stingers.py). out: path from the repo root; the original goes to <game>/assets/originals/music/. Prompts are the ones in each game's music-requests.md. Full songs are made separately by the owner.

stingers.prompt: Instrumental short, happy success jingle for finishing a job and getting paid in a cheerful sandbox game, about 5 seconds, one shot with a natural ending. A bright brass fanfare in B-flat major rising up the scale, a glockenspiel sparkle and a cash-register-like bell ding, a quick drum fill and a final big, bouncy major chord with a cymbal splash. Proud, satisfying and a bit cheesy. No vocals.

Instrumental short comedic out-of-time sting for failing a job in a cheerful sandbox game, about 4 seconds, one shot with a natural ending. A muted trombone slides down wah-wah-waaah, a bassoon bumbles underneath, and it ends on a single soft, wobbly tuba note and a little slide whistle falling away. Funny and sheepish, never harsh or sad. No vocals.

Instrumental short magical you-found-a-present jingle for unlocking a new hat or outfit in a cosy sandbox game, about 3 seconds, one shot with a natural ending. A quick ascending harp glissando, a twinkling glockenspiel and celesta motif in C major, a soft cymbal shimmer, and a final bright bell chord. Delightful and surprising, like opening a gift. No vocals.

A short, triumphant instrumental victory fanfare, about five seconds long, for a cartoon party game about spiders with plasma swords. Bright brass and a whistling synth play a cheeky, celebratory rising motif, backed by a snare roll and a cymbal crash, finishing on a big major chord with a playful glockenspiel sparkle and a quick upward synth whoosh. Joyful, cartoonish and punchy. Clean ending with a natural ring-out, no loop, no vocals.

A short instrumental game over sting, about six seconds long, for a cartoon co-op game where a team of little spiders has been overrun by a swarm of insects. A comic, deflating descending phrase on a muted trombone and a tuba, with a falling pizzicato string run and a buzzing synth swarm that swells and then fades away, ending on a soft, slightly sad minor chord with a single glockenspiel note. Funny and sympathetic rather than gloomy, like a cartoon oh no. Clean ending with a natural ring-out, no loop, no vocals.
